subject: Re: Post-demo: Confirmation of no model learning + ephemeral log policy
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Confirmation of no model learning + ephemeral log policy

Hi Maria — thanks again for the demo slot today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned with Aurum’s privacy requirements: 

1) Training/no-model-learning: Redwood confirms we will not use Aurum customer traffic to further train or fine-tune any public or internal models. No data will be added to training corpora, offline model stores, or used for model improvement without a separate, signed consent.

2) Logging & retention: We agree to an ephemeral logs policy for this pilot — request and response traces retained for 14 days, then deleted unless you request export. Retention applies to both application-level logs and token-level trace artifacts (no long-term KV-cache dumps).

3) PII handling: We will run an automated pseudonymization pass on selectable fields (PII tokenization) before any temporary log export. For the pilot, sampling-based audit logs are available on request.

4) Audit & evidence: Attached is a short PDF (Redwood-Privacy-Commitment.pdf) summarizing the above for legal/security review. If Aurum’s security team needs SOC-2 artifacts, we can pull a limited evidence bundle and provide it via the shared Drive link.

Action items: 
- Maria: confirm that 14-day retention + pseudonymization approach is acceptable for the pilot.
- Ben: I’ve looped you and Laura for pricing/contract overlap (DPA + pilot MSA).
- We will prepare a one-page DPA addendum for signature (DocuSign).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call with security if that helps.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-Privacy-Commitment.pdf (PDF, 32 KB)

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@aurumsystems.com>

Vanessa — appreciate the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from security: 

- When you say "pseudonymization pass", can you confirm which fields are in-scope (we typically need email, phone, and user id masked)? Will the tokenization be reversible by Redwood?
- For the 14-day retention, is there an SLA for deletion? We want deletions to be irreversible and auditable.

If you can provide a short checklist on pseudonymization mechanics and the deletion workflow (who triggers, how we verify), we can sign off on the pilot DPA. Otherwise we may ask for a short security call.

Thanks —
Maria
Product Security Manager
Aurum Systems

Hi Maria — Ben from Solutions here. Short answers to the security questions and how we’ll operationalize the commitments for the pilot: 

- Pseudonymization: we will apply irreversible tokenization for the agreed PII fields (email, phone, user_id) using a one-way hash with salt unique per-customer. Redwood will not retain the salt for pilot exports; salts are rotated and kept within the customer-scoped environment when requested for debugging under a signed exception. In short: standard irreversible tokenization for the pilot unless Aurum requests reversible mapping in writing.

- Deletion SLA: automated lifecycle job will mark eligible logs for deletion at T+14 days and run an irreversible purge routine within 24 hours of marking. We record deletion events to an immutable audit trail (audit record only contains metadata: record id, deletion timestamp, operator id). The actual content payload is purged.

- Who triggers / verify: deletions are automatic; exports must be requested by a named Aurum admin. We can provide a deletion audit CSV on request and also export the audit-record hashes to verify via your security tooling.

Next steps: I’ll draft the DPA addendum language for these points and put it into DocuSign. Vanessa — I’ve started a HubSpot activity (ID: 67890) and attached the draft to the deal. Maria — will ping when DocuSign link is ready.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
